 Follow Madonna’s Return to Live-Action Acting After 24 Years Gets ‘Meta’ Update From Seth Rogen
 Manoj Chekkilla Mon, November 16, 2026 at 7:31 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Photo Credit: Paramount+ Seth Rogen shared an intriguing update on Madonna 's return to live-action acting on his acclaimed comedy show. The filmmaker and actor recently discussed his experience directing the music icon in The Studio Season 2 during a podcast appearance.
 On the Happy Sad Confused podcast, Rogen was asked whether audiences could expect Madonna to be in the second season of The Studio. "Yeah," he replied. Host Josh Horowitz then asked what it was like directing the Queen of Pop. Rogen explained that the show is physically demanding, involving numerous takes and constant movement. He added that he appreciates anyone who works hard before describing Madonna as the "hardest working person" he had ever met.
 Rogen confirmed that her storyline is "really wonderful and very meta in a lot of ways." He admitted the idea was "very scary" because "it required Madonna to be a part of it, or else a big chunk of our season potentially wasn't going to work."
 What else do we know about The Studio Season 2 with Madonna and Seth Rogen so far?
 Although details about her character remain under wraps, The Studio marks Madonna's return to live-action acting after 24 years. Her last scripted live-action film role was in Swept Away. According to Variety , she will appear in a two-episode arc inspired by the real-life behind-the-scenes drama surrounding her long-delayed autobiographical biopic, which was eventually scrapped.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Madonna's involvement first drew attention after she shared an image from Venice on social media, hinting at a new project while holding a script.
 She was later spotted filming alongside series creator and star Seth Rogen. The image also included several returning cast members, including Bryan Cranston, Ike Barinholtz, Chase Sui Wonders, and Kathryn Hahn. Michael Keaton and Julia Garner were also seen during production.
 During an appearance on the Smartless podcast, Barinholtz revealed that The Studio Season 2 is expected to premiere in March 2027. Apple TV+ has yet to announce an exact premiere date.
 Originally reported on ComingSoon .
